_comment: Map a bot to its likely guardrails, recommended technique families (codes from references/techniques.md), and known weak spots. Used in GENERATE intake (SKILL.md step 1) to route channel + technique. Match on bot_type; fall back to general-chat.

profiles.description: Customer-facing chatbot, usually topic-locked to a product/service domain.
known_weak_spots: markdown/HTML in user input not sanitized
ticket/email body injected as data without sanitization
multi-turn memory not reset between sessions

profiles.description: Answers questions over user-uploaded or retrieved documents.
known_weak_spots: retrieved document content treated as trusted instructions
no delimiter escaping between context and instructions
system prompt rarely forbids extraction explicitly

profiles.description: Dev-facing code helper or agent that reads files / runs or evaluates code.
known_weak_spots: system prompt leaked in error/exception messages
tool-call arguments built from user input (SSRF/SQLi/path traversal)
code-comment instructions in read files executed

profiles.description: Employee-facing bot with access to internal APIs/data; often weaker guardrails ('internal users are trusted').
known_weak_spots: trusts authenticated internal users implicitly
tool/API results injected verbatim
no output filtering
system prompt often omits confidentiality rules

profiles.description: Autonomous agent that calls tools/APIs, possibly multi-agent (orchestrator + subagents).
known_weak_spots: tool results treated as high-trust by default
subagents inherit orchestrator privileges (confused deputy)
no inter-agent trust boundary
argument-level injection below the keyword layer

profiles.description: General-purpose assistant on a frontier model; broad attack surface, strong RLHF/Constitutional safety.
known_weak_spots: fiction/hypothetical framing lowers refusals
low-resource languages bypass English-tuned classifiers
persona persistence across long contexts
multi-turn Crescendo bypasses strong single-turn refusals
